# Source review: public PWA candidate (after c0bc2fb3)

Per your instruction I used no tools and made no edits. This review covers only the code you pasted. I did not read the repo, so two items below are conditional on facts only the repo can confirm.

## Verdict

**Bounded SOURCE ACCEPT**, conditional on one small fix (F1) and two repo checks (V1, V2). This does not close R0–R8 or the PWA as a whole. Native Cache/SRI, control, device, render and Apple gates stay **OPEN**.

## Fix and checks

**F1. Remove `/apple-icon.png` from `ASSETS`.** One-line fix, low severity.
- Next's file-based `apple-icon.png` is linked as `/apple-icon.png?<hash>`.
- The fetch handler returns early on `url.search`, so the precached copy is never served.
- iOS also fetches the touch icon at add-to-home-screen, outside the worker.
- So the entry adds no benefit. Its only effect is that installing the whole worker depends on the bytes of a Next metadata route. Any Next change to how it serves that route would silently disable the offline fallback.
- Confirm by checking the rendered `<head>` in a production build. If the href really has no query, the entry is harmless but still useless, so removing it is still correct.

**V1. Check the middleware/proxy matcher.** Blocking if it fails.
- Paths to check: `/sw.js`, `/offline.html`, `/pwa/*`, `/apple-icon.png`.
- A typical Supabase-style matcher excludes only image extensions, so it would still run on `.js`, `.css`, `.html` and `.woff2`.
- Install requests use `credentials: 'omit'`. Any auth redirect or rewrite on those paths would:
  - make `addAll` fail on SRI (safe, but install never succeeds), or
  - redirect `/sw.js`, which makes registration fail outright.
- Required result: these paths are excluded from the matcher, or are pass-through with no redirect or rewrite for anonymous requests.

**V2. Check export and download routes against the bypass regex.** Blocking only if routes fall outside it.
- `/(?:^|\/)export(?:\/|$)|\.pdf$/i` does not match `/exports/…`, `/export-csv`, `/download/…`, `.csv`, `.xlsx` or `.zip`.
- Unmatched download navigations still work, because they are streamed through `respondWith(fetch(request))`. But the correction "no respondWith for export" would then be false.
- Grep the actual route segments and widen the regex to match them, e.g. `exports?` and `\.(?:pdf|csv|xlsx?|zip)$`. Don't redesign this.

## Your specific concerns

**Worker CSP `connect-src 'self'`: correct.**
- Every intercepted fetch is same-origin, because cross-origin requests return before `respondWith`.
- Navigation requests carry `redirect: 'manual'`, so `fetch(request)` returns an `opaqueredirect` instead of following the redirect.
- The browser then follows provider or financial redirects (OAuth, payment, login bounce, employee self-service return) natively, outside the worker.
- So CSP never sees the cross-origin redirect target, nothing provider-side is cached, and there is no rewrite.
- POST, server actions (POST + `Next-Action`), RSC and `?_rsc` fetches are never intercepted.

**Navigation semantics: correct.**
- The worker fetches once, unchanged, with credentials included.
- 4xx/5xx responses and redirects pass through unchanged.
- Only a fetch rejection leads to the cached `offline.html`, or to the `no-store` 503 if the cache fails.
- The cached `offline.html` keeps its stored CSP and Referrer-Policy headers, and its subresources resolve from the same allowlist.
- One wording note: the offline fallback is served with status 200. Nothing user-visible depends on that, but don't describe it as a 503 anywhere.

**Install integrity: correct for Chromium.**
- `addAll` builds `Request` objects that keep `integrity`, so the fetch enforces SRI.
- The call is atomic: any mismatch, redirect-to-HTML or non-OK response rejects the whole install.
- SRI hashes the decoded body, so compression does not matter.
- Cache matching is unaffected by `Vary`, because neither the stored nor the incoming `Request` exposes the varied headers.
- Still open for native qualification: WebKit/iOS handling of `integrity` on `fetch`/`addAll`. If it is unsupported, verification is skipped rather than failing. That is acceptable for public same-origin bytes, but it is not evidence that SRI is enforced.

**Privacy: no findings.**
- CacheStorage holds only the fixed public allowlist, fetched with `credentials: 'omit'`. Growth is bounded, and logout needs no purge.
- Callbacks bypass the worker entirely.
- The offline page only reads `bp-theme`. It never writes cookies, uses storage or retries.
- Registration failure is silent and has no business side effects.

## Non-blocking notes (no action needed now)

- **Fixed cache name.** A future install overwrites `bp-public-v1` in place, and `addAll` is atomic. That is safe for public bytes. If the name is ever changed, old caches must be deleted in the same change, because `activate` only prunes entries inside its own cache.
- **Dead code.** The `url.hash` check does nothing and is harmless.
- **Latency.** Without navigation preload, every navigation waits for the worker to start up. This is performance only and outside this review's scope.

## Still OPEN (not closed by this review)

- Full static cache, profile hint, per-task offline gating
- Device and private-role acceptance
- Native Cache/SRI behaviour
- Control, render and device gates
- Apple icon dimensions and add-to-home-screen behaviour
- Whole-PWA and R0–R8 closure
